name: Han nationalism
summary: Han nationalism is an ethnic nationalism that treats ethnic Han Chinese as the core, or only true members, of the Chinese nation. It arose in the late Qing as an anti-Manchu revolutionary creed that framed Han and Manchu as rival races and sought a republic, and it survives as a cultural and online movement such as the Hanfu revival and as Han-centrism inside state nationalism. It often conflicts with the official multi-ethnic idea of the Chinese nation.
scope: The late Qing revolutionary core, based on Zou Rong's The Revolutionary Army (1903) and Zhang Binglin's racial writings, plus the modern cultural and online strand (Hanfu movement, Han-centrism, resentment of minority preferences). Han Taiwanese nationalism and the CCP's critique of 'Han chauvinism' are noted but not the basis. Economic and social-policy questions were mostly never addressed, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Economic welfare is not part of the doctrine; the Han-as-nation framing leans toward a state that looks after its core people, so a weak lean to agree is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Sources describe Han nationalism through race and nation, not wage policy, and adherents range from state-socialist to market views.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The doctrine takes no economic line; Zou Rong's republican program lists no market policy and modern adherents split between state-led and market positions.

public-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the ethnic-nationalist core addresses ownership of utilities, and adherents are divided.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Zou Rong's program says everyone bears the burden of taxation but sets no progressive rate; later adherents have no common line.

unions-good.rationale: Labor organization is outside what the sources define as Han nationalism; adherents are split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Zou Rong lists natural rights including life and freedoms but the sources give no firm stance on how inviolable property is.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No documented position; the movement's concerns are ethnic and national, not corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed in sources; Han-nationalist online discourse resents minority preferences but takes no clear line on welfare as such.

worker-ownership.rationale: Class-based collective ownership is foreign to a movement that defines the nation by ethnicity, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Strong-state, security-minded nationalism, with Han chauvinism fused to state nationalism in the PRC context, makes tolerance of surveillance the likelier answer, but it is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Late Qing nationalists cast opium as a mark of national weakness and the moral-order outlook of modern adherents is conservative; inferred, not stated.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents defend openly ethnocentric speech and resent laws that shield minorities, so they likely oppose such restrictions; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Han-centric nationalism has been fused with state nationalism under strong leaders such as Xi Jinping, but the early revolutionaries sought elected republics; mild and contested.

state-harmful.rationale: The tradition is state-building: Zou Rong demands a new central government and republic, so the state is essential, not harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Zou Rong wants every man to serve as a citizen soldier, but modern Han nationalists work within a state that restricts guns; inferred and weak.

empower-police-military.rationale: The program stresses national independence and citizen soldiers, and Han nationalism links to resistance against foreign powers; a modest lean to agree.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Hanfu strand stresses Confucian moral self-cultivation and conservative norms, so legalization is unlikely; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Zou Rong calls for a central government as general body for the whole Han nation, and the movement is unitary nationalist, so decentralization is disfavored.

rehabilitation.rationale: No documented stance on penal philosophy; adherents are divided.

traditional-family.rationale: The Hanfu strand ties revival to Confucian ritual and moral self-cultivation, supporting traditional family values as part of Han cultural heritage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Traditionalist Confucian cultural revival leans against it, though the sources do not state a position; inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: No documented position; adherents split between pronatalist and pragmatic views.

more-religion-public.rationale: Han nationalists favor Confucian and folk heritage but are not defined by religious public life; revival is cultural, and some online strands are hostile to Islam and Tibetan Buddhism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents resent affirmative action and legal leniency for ethnic minorities, so they reject state remedial programs framed around ethnicity.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Traditionalist cultural revival leans toward natural gender roles; the sources do not say, so this is inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Reviving Han clothing, rites and heritage is the centre of the Hanfu movement and Han cultural nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: The founding texts call for sweeping away millennia of despotism by revolution, not gradual reform; Zhang Binglin opposed Liang Qichao's reformism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The movement guards the Han core of the nation and links to anxiety about outsiders, but immigration into China is not discussed in the sources; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Zou Rong demands independence and no foreign interference with Chinese affairs, so ceding power to international bodies runs against the tradition.

free-trade.rationale: The founding texts resent harassment by the foreign Powers but no trade doctrine is stated; adherents are split.

nation-first.rationale: The Revolutionary Army puts Han racial survival and national independence above all else, against the Powers and Manchu rule.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Zou Rong opposes any intervention in China and the movement is wary of foreign interference, so it likely extends that logic to others; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: A nation defined by Han ethnicity and bloodline rejects open borders as incompatible with preserving it.

limit-growth.rationale: National strength and rejuvenation are central, so limits on growth are disfavored; the sources do not discuss environment.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No documented stance; not part of the ideology.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Zou Rong credits scientific advance with destroying superstition and despotism, so a mild pro-progress lean.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Modern Han nationalism backs national strength and development, and nothing in it opposes nuclear power; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: The founding text is a call to revolution, and Zou Rong says people may overthrow a government that infringes their rights.

experts-over-public.rationale: No clear stance; revolutionaries favored elected assemblies while later Han-centrism fused with state authority.

central-planning.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range across economic views.

socialized-markets.rationale: No documented stance on enterprise ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; Sun Yat-sen's land-value ideas belong to a wider revolutionary program rather than Han nationalism proper.

tax-inheritance.rationale: None of the sources opened for this audit records a Han-nationalist position on this, so adherents are treated as split.

basic-income.rationale: No stance recorded; outside the movement's concerns.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Resentment of foreign Powers and emphasis on national independence point to mild protectionism, but it is inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Fusion with state nationalism and the Chinese Dream of rejuvenation favor strategic state direction; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed. (inferred from the movement's core claims)

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A nation-centred, ethnically defined movement has no program of abolishing money or wage labor.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Adherents back strong state institutions, so abolition is unlikely; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Early revolutionaries wanted an elected republic, while the modern Han-centric strand is fused with CCP-state nationalism; adherents split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Zou Rong calls for killing the Manchu emperor as a warning that despotism must not revive and for a republic.

democracy-best.rationale: The founding text envisions elected assemblies and a president, yet modern online Han nationalists are divided and often ethnically conditional about democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Zou Rong proposes elected deputies and public elections, not direct legislation by citizens.

workers-councils.rationale: The program is a republic with elected deputies on national lines, not class-based councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Han nationalists see Tibet, Xinjiang, Mongolia and Taiwan as part of the nation or its sphere and oppose separation.

natural-rulers.rationale: Han racial superiority narratives exist but the sources do not state a doctrine of natural rulers for individuals.

political-violence-never.rationale: Zou Rong calls for expelling or killing the Manchus and the emperor, treating violence as legitimate.

war-builds-character.rationale: The founding text glorifies revolution and martial duty, with all men as citizen soldiers, but a general claim about war is inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: No stance stated; the movement is cultural rather than religious.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Zou Rong grounds law in natural rights and public agreement, and the strand is not scripture-based.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The program demands a central state with citizen soldiers, leaving no room for privatized defense.

military-superiority.rationale: Han nationalism pursues national strength and rejects the humiliation by foreign powers; PRC Han-centrism supports military power.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The defining claim is that ethnic Han are the true members of the Chinese nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement sees history in terms of race and nation, not class; Zhang Binglin framed conflict as Han versus Manchu.

equal-outcomes.rationale: No egalitarian economic program; ethnic hierarchy within the nation sits uneasily with this.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Han nationalists reject autonomy claims by Tibetans, Uyghurs and Mongols over their traditional lands.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Zou Rong resents foreign domination but no reparations demand appears in the sources; inferred as split.

civilizational-union.rationale: Han nationalism is ethnic, not civilizational, though some strands extend to a wider Han family; mild disagreement.

self-interest-moral.rationale: None of the sources opened for this audit records a Han-nationalist position on this, so adherents are treated as split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Zou Rong stresses both natural rights and citizen duties of soldiering and taxation; the Confucian strand leans to duty but the question is mixed.

limit-population.rationale: No stance; Han nationalism worries about Han racial survival, which cuts against limits, while PRC policy imposed them.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The tradition embraces science and modern progress to renew the nation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pro-science but institutional continuity matters to the cultural strand; no clear position.

human-enhancement.rationale: None of the sources opened for this audit records a Han-nationalist position on this, so adherents are treated as split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: None of the sources opened for this audit records a Han-nationalist position on this, so adherents are treated as split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: None of the sources opened for this audit records a Han-nationalist position on this, so adherents are treated as split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage revival is the center of the Hanfu movement; sacrificing it is opposite.

dominated-front.rationale: Zou Rong sees China harassed by the Powers, and Han nationalism includes resistance to Western imperialism; no documented call for a common front.

workers-nation.rationale: Nation-first ethnic nationalism holds that people organize as a nation rather than as an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Zou Rong declares men and women equal, but the traditionalist Hanfu strand leans conservative; split.

ban-interest.rationale: No documented stance; inferred disagree as unrelated to the movement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Han racism targets Manchus and minorities but the sources do not describe segregation laws; Zhang Binglin sought expulsion, so mild disagree only.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The nationalist view of the state is as an ethnic instrument, not a class tool, so mild disagreement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: National economic strength has priority; no stated position, so inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Han-centrism expects minorities and newcomers to adopt Han culture; the article describes Han civilising narratives and sinicization of Xinjiang.

elite-replacement.rationale: The sources do not document a replacement conspiracy theory for Han nationalism; some strands do blame elites for minority preferences.

proportional-representation.rationale: Zou Rong proposes elected deputies from each province without specifying electoral system.

national-mission.rationale: Han nationalism emphasizes the Han nation, not spreading a regime abroad, though civilising narratives exist.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Zou Rong declares equality but the movement does not use structural-patriarchy analysis; weak disagree.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Zou Rong denounces the Manchu court and Qing elite as corrupt and tyrannical; the modern strand frames elites as corrupt toward minorities.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Racial nationalism and social Darwinism could support this, but it is not documented; split.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Strong-state nationalism dislikes prosecution of its own forces, though not stated.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement wants a strong state defending nation and heritage, beyond night-watchman role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The movement values Han bloodline purity and Han nationalists oppose assimilation of others into the nation; Zhang Binglin stressed bloodline.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Han racial hierarchy over Manchus and minorities conflicts with equal rights before the law, though Zou Rong asserts equality among Han citizens.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not part of the ideology; nationalism favors national road.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Han settlement into Tibet, Xinjiang and Inner Mongolia is framed by adherents as legitimate national migration, so they reject this label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Han-centric view opposes special legal treatment for minorities and wants one law for all.

restrict-conversion.rationale: No stance recorded; some online Han nationalists oppose Islam's spread, others are indifferent.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not part of Han practice; beef consumption is common and the cause is Hindu.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: None of the sources opened for this audit records a Han-nationalist position on this, so adherents are treated as split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state question outside the ideology.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Zou Rong says governments rest on public agreement and may be overthrown when they infringe rights, though the consent is that of Han people.

trade-surplus.rationale: National strength and independence from Powers suggest mild mercantilism, but nothing is stated.

population-transfer.rationale: Zou Rong and Zhang Binglin called for expelling the Manchus; Zhang preferred expulsion to Manchuria.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The founding text calls for expelling or killing Manchus and the emperor, which is initiating force.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: None of the sources opened for this audit records a Han-nationalist position on this, so adherents are treated as split.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Social spending is not addressed in the sources; adherents are split.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the late Qing programme sought a republic with citizen participation, not leader-centred bypassing of parties.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the republican, natural-rights programme; not directly stated.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from the Han-centred cultural strand and Hanfu movement, which stress heritage over religious groupings.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Hanfu movement links modern life with revival of Confucian and ancestral heritage, but this is inferred from a reference article.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not discuss divorce, but the modern movement does not oppose it.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from nationalism opposed to alien rule; resource control is not addressed in the sources.

missingStatements.text: The ruling dynasty or elite of a different ethnic origin than the majority has no legitimate claim to rule the nation.
missingStatements.rationale: The anti-Manchu revolution rested on branding the Qing as an alien race, and Zou Rong called for overthrowing the Manchu government.

missingStatements.text: The people should adopt the traditional dress and rites of their ancestors in preference to those imposed or influenced by foreign rulers.
missingStatements.rationale: The Hanfu movement revives pre-Qing dress over qipao and tangzhuang, which it links to Manchu rule.

missingStatements.text: The nation descends from a common ancestor, and that bloodline is the basis of its identity.
missingStatements.rationale: Zou Rong calls Han the descendants of the Yellow Emperor and Zhang Binglin stressed Han bloodline.

notes: Han nationalism is distinct from official Chinese nationalism, whose multi-ethnic framing the CCP defends, and the PRC treats 'Han chauvinism' as a fault. Han Taiwanese nationalism diverges on unification. Few of the 312 statements touch the movement's concerns, so most answers are inferred and low-confidence.
